option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: anthro mutations
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded anthro animal mutation fangs bite teeth beast
option.helptext:
Adds this fork's animal-trait mutations to the physical mutation list.
Qud's physical mutations are full of things that make you stranger - a carapace, quills, a beak, an extra pair of legs. What it has almost none of is the ordinary animal end of that: the traits a wolf or a cat has and a person does not.
Currently three mutations:
Fangs, 3 points. Long teeth on your face that bite alongside whatever you are wielding, roughly one round in five, and draw blood when they land. They do not occupy your face slot, so a mask or goggles still fit.
Bleeding is normally bought - Bloodletter costs 150 skill points and needs Agility 17. Fangs give you a smaller share of it for a mutation point instead, and the two stack if you have both.
Keen Smell, 3 points. You detect creatures around you by scent, at roughly twice the range of Heightened Hearing - but walls stop a smell dead, and a closed door, deep water or anything blocking your view cuts it down. Better in open country than in a ruin, which is the opposite of hearing.
Keen Smell is Caves of Qud's own Heightened Smell. Freehold built it, gave it to a few animals, and never put it in the list you pick from. This puts it there.
Tail, 1 point. A tail. It gives you 1 DV, and when something would knock you down you get an Agility save to keep your feet - so it helps more the nimbler you are. It does not attack and it cannot hold anything, and an axe can cut it off, which takes the dodge with it.
Pick which tail at character creation - fox, wolf, cat, rat or lizard. That choice is pure flavour; they all behave the same.
Turning this off hides the mutations at character creation and keeps them off randomly generated creatures. Mutations are read while a character is being made, so this applies to a NEW character - an existing one keeps whatever it was born with.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: graded burden
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded burden encumbrance weight carry capacity overburdened
option.helptext:
Makes carrying weight a gradient instead of a cliff.
Vanilla has one threshold: carry more than 15 pounds per point of Strength and you become Overburdened, which means unable to move at all. Below that, nothing. So the best play is to sit just under the limit forever and never think about it again.
With this on, four bands sit underneath that threshold:
Lightly burdened, at half capacity - minus 1 DV. Encumbered, at three quarters - minus 2 DV. Heavily burdened, at nine tenths - minus 4 DV, minus 10 Quickness, and you cannot run.
Vanilla's Overburdened is untouched and still stops you dead at full capacity. What changes is that you feel the weight coming before it stops you.
Player only, as in vanilla, where no NPC is ever overburdened at any load.
Safe to switch on or off mid-run: the band is recalculated every turn.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Mutated Human mutation points
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded mutation points mutant chargen
option.helptext:
How many mutation points a Mutated Human starts character creation with.
Vanilla Caves of Qud gives 12. Caves of Qud Expanded has always given 16, which is the default here.
{{y|Set this before creating a character.}} Changing it has no effect on a character that already exists.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Mutated Human hit points per level
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded mutation hit points hp level mutant health
option.helptext:
How many hit points a Mutated Human rolls each level, applied from your next level onward.
{{G|1-5}} is this mod's: swingier than vanilla, with a higher ceiling. {{y|2-3}} is what version 2.2 shipped, apparently by mistake. {{y|1-4}} is vanilla's.
True Kin and Psionic Adepts are unaffected.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: extra skill points per level
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded skill points level gain mutant true kin
option.helptext:
Grants the extra skill points per level this mod has always given: {{G|65}} for a Mutated Human against vanilla's 50, and {{G|85}} for a True Kin against vanilla's 70.
Turn this off to earn exactly vanilla's. It applies from your next level and never takes back points you have earned. Psionic Adepts are unaffected.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: extra starting skills
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded starting skills chargen cooking staunch wounds

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: eased skill requirements
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded skill requirements attribute axe cudgel long blade multiweapon en garde

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: retuned skill point costs
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded skill point cost tinkering cooking butchery spicer reverse engineer
option.helptext:
Keeps this mod's skill point prices: {{W|Reverse Engineer}} {{G|200}}, and {{W|Butchery}} and {{W|Spicer}} {{G|100}} each.
The Cooking prices pay for the free skills {{W|extra starting skills}} grants, so if that is off you may want this off too. Applies immediately.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: starting reputation bonus
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded starting reputation joppa faction chargen

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: home base building in Joppa
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded joppa building home base becoming nook
option.helptext:
Adds a walled building near Argyve's workshop in Joppa: a bed, storage, an oven, and a becoming nook with a cybernetics rack.
{{y|Takes effect when you restart the game, and applies to Joppa as it is first generated.}} A character who already has the building keeps it, and one made without it will not gain it later - Joppa is built once, and what it was built with is in the save.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: ask a creature its name
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded ask name conversation npc creature introduce naming
option.helptext:
Adds {{G|What is your name?}} to conversations with creatures that have no name yet, and they answer.
Most of the people in Qud already have names - the game just never gave you a way to ask. A snapjaw answers with a snapjaw name, an Issachari raider with an Issachari one, because the name is drawn from their own culture, faction and region the same way a village elder's is.
The question is asked a different way each time, and what they say back is Caves of Qud's own wording.
{{y|Asking means you can no longer rename them.}} The game refuses to rename anyone who already has a name - {{y|"doesn't want a new name."}} - so a creature that has told you who it is cannot be given a name by you afterwards. Asking who someone is and deciding who they are are different things, and this makes you choose. Turn this off if you would rather name your companions yourself.
Applies immediately. Names already given are kept.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Trash Divining runs dry as a zone is picked over
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded trash divining secrets rifle garbage scavenging density diminishing
option.helptext:
Makes a zone's trash run out of things to tell you, instead of paying the same rate for all hundred piles.
{{Y|Trash Divining}} rolls a 5% chance per pile, which sounds like a trickle and is not. The catacombs lay down 80 to 100 piles in a single zone, so rifling one of them hands you four or five secrets - and secrets are worth 50 reputation each at a water ritual.
With this on, the {{Y|5%}} is untouched and the first twenty piles in a zone still pay it in full. After that the same zone drops to {{Y|3%}}, then {{Y|2%}}, then {{Y|1%}}, and never lower. A catacombs zone pays around two secrets rather than four or five. Thin zones are left alone - a rustwell has too few piles to reach the second band, and pays what it always did.
The count is kept per zone, so walking out and back does not reset it, and the piles you already went through are gone regardless.
Applies immediately, and keeps counting while it is off - turning it off in a rich zone and on again will not hand you a fresh 5%.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Mind's Compass reports your bearings
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded wayfaring minds compass parasang bearings zone navigation
option.helptext:
Lets Mind's Compass tell you which of a parasang's nine zones you are standing in.
A parasang is a 3x3 block of zones and the game never says which one you are in, so you work it out by walking to an edge and watching which way the world map scrolls. With this on, you are told when you arrive, under the line where the game already gives you the zone and the time: {{G|The northeast of this parasang.}} And so on through the nine.
You need {{Y|Mind's Compass}}, which comes free with the {{Y|Wayfaring}} skill rather than being bought separately.
Nothing is said while you are {{y|lost}} - that is the one time you should not know - or on the world map, or anywhere without one. Going down stairs is silent too, since a staircase does not move you within the parasang.
Applies immediately.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: psionic chips in loot
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded psionic chip drops loot artifact tables
option.helptext:
Lets psionic chips and chipsets appear in the world, rolled from the artifact tables at tiers 3 through 8.
Turn this off for the mod's weapons, armor and genotypes without the chip economy - no chip can be tinkered, so this closes the supply. Applies immediately.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: True Kin Chip Interface slots
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded chip interface slot chargen psionic implant true kin
option.helptext:
Gives a True Kin the {{G|2}} Chip Interface slots this mod grants them. Psionic Adepts are unaffected - their {{G|4}} are the genotype. A Mutated Human has none either way: chips grant mutations to genotypes that cannot mutate, and that one can.
{{y|Set this before creating a character.}} A body is built once, at character creation, so this cannot change a character who already exists.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Chip Interface slots on other humanoids
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded chip interface npc humanoid anatomy world
option.helptext:
Gives every other humanoid a Chip Interface slot, merged into the base humanoid anatomy. Nothing here puts a chip in an NPC's slot, so leaving it on has no effect you can see. Your own slots are the option above.
{{y|Set this before creating a character.}} Bodies are built once, when a creature is generated.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: wider name pools
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded name names naming repeat repetition syllable prefix postfix
option.helptext:
Adds syllables to the Qudish name pools, so procedurally generated people stop sounding alike.
Vanilla draws from 29 openings and 24 endings, which is about 93,500 distinct names - so it is not the whole name you notice repeating, it is the syllable. There is a 50% chance of seeing a repeated opening after fewer than seven names. This takes openings to 68 and endings to 36, which moves that to eleven.
The middle syllables are deliberately left nearly alone. That is not where the collision is.
{{y|Issachari names are widened the opposite way, and for the opposite reason.}} An Issachari is one hyphenated phrase - {{G|Flays-upon-the-Sun}}, {{G|Chokes-in-Quicksalt}} - drawn from 7 verbs, 5 prepositions and 8 nouns. That is 280 names, so here it is the whole name that repeats, at around twenty people, and every single slot repeats at three or four. All three pools widen together to 10, 10 and 12, which is 1,200 names and a repeat at about forty.
Turning this off restores vanilla's pools exactly. Nothing vanilla is removed or reweighted either way.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: gendered name endings
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded name names naming gender feminine soft ending vowel
option.helptext:
Lets a generated person's name reflect the gender the game already gave them.
Qud rolls a gender for almost every human it generates - 117 of the 126 human blueprints are a male-or-female coin flip - and then ignores it when naming them. Vanilla's endings are 23 hard stops out of 24, so everyone ends up sounding the same way regardless.
With this on, women draw mostly from open, vowel-final endings and the genders that are neither draw from an even mix. It is a lean rather than a rule: about one name in five still takes a hard ending, so a name never states someone's gender outright.
Turning this off makes naming gender-blind again, as vanilla is. It does not narrow the pools - that is the option above.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: how your own random name sounds
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded name random player character masc femme sound rename
option.helptext:
Chooses which pool your character's name is drawn from when the game rolls one for you, rather than you typing one in.
Masc gives the hard-stopped endings vanilla has always used. Femme gives the open, vowel-final ones. Random splits evenly between those two and a mixed pool, which is what you get if you never touch this.
It does nothing at all if you type a name in, which is always the surest way to get the one you want. Re-rolling a random name in character creation does follow it, so you can keep pressing until you like what you see.
It follows you afterwards too. Renaming yourself in game draws from the same pool rather than from whatever your gender would suggest, and changing this mid-run takes effect on your next rename.
It does not touch anyone else in the world. The two naming options above govern them.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: choose your gender at character creation
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded gender chargen character creation pronoun nonbinary trans
option.helptext:
Adds a Gender row to character creation.
Qud has thirteen genders with full grammar, and ships every one of them written and switched off - there is no way to pick yours, so the game rolls one for you. This turns the row on, and widens what it offers from four to thirteen: elverson (ey/em), xe, ze, sie, fae, spivak (e/em), ve, per and ne join male, female, neuterperson and nonspecific.
The hindren third gender is deliberately not offered. It is theirs, not a general one.
Turning this off hides the row again and the game picks for you, as vanilla does. The genders themselves stay declared either way, so a character who already has one keeps it.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: choose your pronouns at character creation
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded pronoun pronouns chargen character creation neopronoun they
option.helptext:
Adds a Pronoun Set row to character creation, separate from gender.
Qud tracks pronouns apart from gender, so you can take a gender's grammar and a different set of pronouns. The row defaults to "from gender", which is what you want unless you want something else.
Vanilla ships this switched off too. On, it offers fourteen sets - the three Qud already wrote and never showed anyone, plus one for each gender.
Turning it off hides the row. Your pronouns then follow your gender, as vanilla does it.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: creature colour variants
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded creature variants colour color coat spawn regional biome
option.helptext:
Adds 44 colour and name variants of nineteen common creatures - brindle and marsh dogs, black goats, rust beetles, sorrel equimaxes, hoary bats - each in the biome its name argues for.
Cosmetic only. A variant differs in name, colour and description and in nothing else, so a pied dog fights exactly as a feral dog does.
Each sits below its vanilla parent in the spawn tables, so ordinary animals stay the common ones and a variant is the occasional find rather than the rule.
Applies immediately, to zones generated from now on. Zones you have already visited keep whatever they were built with.
